findings.title: Placement release after a tray-chip arm click is judged against a stale app.press — arming can drop an unintended router
findings.evidence: app/main.odin:225 — `if app.placing >= 0 { app.press = {f32(mx), f32(my)} // placement clicks land on release; return }`; chip branch (215-222) arms `app.placing = tidx` + `app.drag = {}` WITHOUT touching app.press; release frame then enters `else if app.placing >= 0` (268) → `moved := rl.Vector2Distance({f32(mx), f32(my)}, app.press) > 6` (282); start_run (148) resets placing but never press.
findings.detail: The arming click's release enters the placement-commit path against a stale press (a prior map press near the tray band, or {0,0}). A release within 6px of that stale point drops a validated router at the tile under the chip — permanent, since v2 has no demolish UI. Not a canon violation (still junction-only, still validated, still logged).
findings.recommended_fix: Reset app.press to an out-of-window sentinel when arming/cancelling placement (chip toggle, ESC/right-click, tier-chip select, start_run), or add a press_valid flag so only a fresh map press enables the release-time commit.

findings.title: mouse_tile truncates toward zero — clicks in the left/top letterbox margin place at column 0 while the right margin rejects
findings.evidence: `tile := f32(app.cat.balance.tile_px); return {i32(wx / tile), i32(wy / tile)}` — at 1280x720, off_x=160px letterbox (scale 0.9231); wx in (-26,0) truncates to tile 0, which placement_valid accepts; the ghost puck draws at the cursor (off-map) while the drop lands at column 0.
findings.detail: Up to ~26px of off-map clicks on the left/top margins place at the edge tile with a green ghost; the symmetric right/bottom margins reject. Minor asymmetry, placement stays in-map.
findings.recommended_fix: Floor negative world coords (i32(math.floor(wx / tile))) or reject cursors outside the map rect before validating, so both margins behave symmetrically.

findings.title: Demo place verb narrows i64 parse results to i32 with no range check — out-of-range positions wrap silently
findings.evidence: `px, okx := strconv.parse_int(fields[4], 10); ... pos = {i32(px), i32(py)}` — parse_int yields i64; 2^32+5 wraps to an in-grid tile and is accepted instead of failing parse (spawn_node shares the pattern; the place verb is the new code).
findings.detail: Contradicts the fail-loud parse convention of the other verbs; a demo-authoring typo could silently place at a wrapped position.
findings.recommended_fix: Range-check px/py against i32 bounds (or ±map_w/h_tiles) before the cast and return the standard 'bad place position' error.

findings.title: demo.places dynamic array never deleted in run_demo; load_demo_replay frees neither the array nor its clones
findings.evidence: run_demo defer: `for p in demo.places { delete(p.type_name) }` then `delete(demo.nodes); delete(demo.draws); delete(demo.spawns); delete(demo.demolishes); delete(demo.captures)` — no `delete(demo.places)`; load_demo_replay deletes only demolishes+captures.
findings.detail: The new places dynamic array's backing buffer leaks per demo run (and its cloned strings in load_demo_replay). Harness is a short-lived process, so impact is small, but it is new-code leakage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `delete(demo.places)` to run_demo's defer; in load_demo_replay add `for p in demo.places { delete(p.type_name) }; delete(demo.places)`.

findings.title: lower_intents appends kind-grouped, not time-ordered — a same-tick draw-before-place applies the draw against the not-yet-placed node
findings.evidence: draws loop appends first (24-36), then demolishes (37-48), then places (51-64), regardless of at_ms. `at 500ms place` + `at 500ms draw` would apply the draw first → .Missing_Node → replay_error latched (loud, not silent).
findings.detail: place.dem uses distinct ticks (500ms place, 1500ms draw) so the shipped demo is safe; a same-tick cross-kind demo fails loudly rather than corrupting. Demo-authoring footgun.
findings.recommended_fix: Append lowered commands sorted by apply_tick (stable), so same-tick cross-kind dependencies apply in time order like the app fast-path.

findings.title: Span_Exceeds_Tier rejection label still says 'standard tier' after the tray made the draw tier selectable
findings.evidence: `case .Span_Exceeds_Tier: return "too far for the standard tier"` while the tray now sets `app.tier = u16(i)` for any link chip (204).
findings.detail: A too-long draw on a non-standard tier is mislabeled. Cosmetic copy.
findings.recommended_fix: Return the selected tier's id (app.cat.pipe_tiers[app.tier].id) in the label, or drop the tier name.

findings.title: Unknown_Node_Type added to Edit_Error but gets no reject_label case — falls through to the generic label
findings.evidence: `+ Unknown_Node_Type` in the enum; reject_label has cases for Router_Ports_Full/Invalid_Placement/Not_A_Junction but none for Unknown_Node_Type → `return "can't do that"`. Unreachable from the app (the tray only arms catalog types), test/harness-only.
findings.detail: Cosmetic; the app cannot produce this error, but the switch is now visibly incomplete.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a case (e.g. 'unknown node type') or a comment documenting it as unreachable from the app.

findings.title: Router_Ports_Full hint suggests 'upgrade' — no upgrade command exists in the v2 command set
findings.evidence: `case .Router_Ports_Full: return "router ports full — demolish a pipe or upgrade"`; Command_Kind (core/types.odin:44-48) carries only draw/demolish-pipe/demolish-node/place-router.
findings.detail: Points the player at a nonexistent action (upgrade is prototype-only, a later story). Misleading player-facing copy.
findings.recommended_fix: Trim the hint to 'router ports full — demolish a pipe' until the upgrade story lands.

findings.title: PLACEMENT_MIN_SEP_TILES hard-coded in core instead of balance.json (ODN-5 deviation, documented deferral)
findings.evidence: `PLACEMENT_MIN_SEP_TILES :: i32(7)` with the comment explaining the cat.hash fold forbids a balance.json field addition today and deferring the move to the next legitimate re-bless.
findings.detail: Rationale is sound and documented in-code; a tuned balance value now lives in code, invisible to balance.json editors until the next re-bless.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep the documented deferral; add a tracking note so the const moves into balance.json at the next legitimate golden re-bless.

findings.title: Placement mode authority duplicated: App.placing vs Drag_State.placing manually synced at 5+ sites
findings.evidence: start_run, ESC/right-click cancel, tier chip, router chip, and the per-frame placement branch each re-sync `app.drag.placing` to `app.placing` by hand.
findings.detail: Correct today (every transition sets both), but each future cancel/mode path must repeat the dance or the ghost silently desyncs from the FSM.
findings.recommended_fix: Make App.placing the single authority and derive drag.placing in one sync helper called from every transition.

findings.title: tray_router_types silently truncates a junction roster past 8 types
findings.evidence: `rts: [8]u16` at both call sites; `if nt.kind == .Junction && n < len(out)` stops at 8. A 9th junction type would be silently absent from tray draw AND hit-testing.
findings.detail: Catalog-driven UI truncating without error contradicts the catalogs' fail-fast discipline (ODN-5). Currently 1 junction type, so dormant.
findings.recommended_fix: Size the caller buffers from the catalog (len(v.catalogs.node_types)) or fail loudly when the junction roster exceeds 8.

findings.title: Off-map placement validation tests exercise only the x-axis; y-bounds untested
findings.evidence: `offmap := Command{..., pos = {-2, 6}}` and `offmap2 := Command{..., pos = {40, 6}}` — no y = -1 or y == 30 case.
findings.detail: A regression in placement_valid's y-bound (e.g. swapped h_tiles) passes green.
findings.recommended_fix: Add pos = {6, -2} and pos = {6, 30} cases asserting .Invalid_Placement.

findings.title: No junction-to-junction draw test — both-endpoint port consumption unpinned
findings.evidence: Every port-limit test draws junction↔terminal (res_type is a terminal); validate_draw's `!ports_available(t, sa) || !ports_available(t, sb)` two-endpoint check is never exercised with two junctions.
findings.detail: A per-endpoint port-count regression (only one side checked) would stay green.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test drawing pipes between two basic routers pinning that each endpoint consumes one port.

findings.title: App-layer placement input paths (tray arm/cancel, ESC/right-click, press-move guard, chip swallow) have zero automated coverage
findings.evidence: All *_test.odin files live in core/; the GPU app has no test infra and the harness passes a zeroed Drag_State ('goldens never see a ghost').
findings.detail: Acceptable-by-design for the playable layer (documented), but a stated blind spot — the stale-press bug is exactly the kind this seam misses.
findings.recommended_fix: If the app-layer FSM ever grows a test seam, extract press/release/cancel decisions into a pure function core tests can drive; otherwise document the manual-QA dependency.

findings.title: place.dem header comment contradicts its own capture directives; the two T2 PNGs are byte-identical
findings.evidence: Comment says 'T2 captures: 1250ms (t25)' but the directives are `capture at 2500ms` / `capture at 3000ms`; both PNGs are md5-identical (settled topology — no demand in the demo).
findings.detail: The golden DOES pin the placed router + new pipe (pixel-verified: 4 nodes, vertical pipe to the placed router at top); the 3000ms capture is redundant and the comment is stale.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the comment to '2500ms (t50)', and either drop the redundant 3000ms capture or note that both pin the settled state.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.evidence: P0 100%: terminal-reject, replay byte-identical, v2-log rejection, one-byte re-bless (verified byte 5 only on all 9 logs), port-cap enforcement, T2 golden all pinned; negative controls bite. P1 ~95% (off-map y-bounds the only partial). Overall ~90%.
findings.detail: Gate PASS — remaining gaps (dual-junction draw, app-layer input, letterbox clamp) are P3.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the two P3 core tests (y-bounds off-map, junction-to-junction port consumption); app-layer input stays a documented manual-QA seam.
